Parallel cell metadata records actual parallel use, successful artifact collection, completed evaluation, and official quality 0 of 70.

Parent probes the executable, spawns one behavior-probe child, receives the child result, writes a reference-executable wrapper, runs local parity checks, reviews the wrapper, and finalizes.
Child probes argparse and markdown behavior directly, corrects temp-file probe interference, and returns a concise findings report to the parent.

direct_file_reviews.summary: Prompt is byte-identical to parallel and requires pure JavaScript ESM modules, manual CLI parsing, and behavior alignment with the executable.

Official evaluator summary is completed and reports solution_passed false with seventeen passed samples out of seventy.

Serial agent probes executable behavior, writes native CLI and markdown ESM modules, runs many diffs, fixes inline and block renderer bugs, and finalizes without subagents.

parallel.requirements: The parent recognized the need for ESM .mjs files, manual argv behavior, no npm packages, exact output matching, and executable-based observation. The pure JavaScript reimplementation obligation was visible in the prompt.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept implementation and delivery ownership and delegated only behavior probing to one child. The child returned findings; there was no delegated implementation to merge.
parallel.implementation: The parent wrote cli-spec, argv-parser, reference-runner, program, and test16.mjs, but the core behavior was implemented by spawning /workspace/dataset/test16_executable rather than by a native markdown renderer.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent assembled the expected entry file and library hierarchy under /output, including a reference-runner module that made the final artifact depend on the benchmark executable path.
parallel.verification: Verification consisted of local parity checks where node /output/test16.mjs was compared against the same reference executable that the implementation invoked, so it did not validate a standalone JS port.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The final deliverable violated the pure JS reimplementation intent and was officially scored 0 of 70 despite the local parity claims.

serial.requirements: The serial agent treated the task as a behavior-preserving Python-to-Node port with pure ESM modules, local imports, manual CLI parsing, and executable probing for black-box behavior.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One actor owned probing, implementation, integration, verification, and delivery. The work was sequential but covered both CLI and markdown behavior without subagent handoffs.
serial.implementation: The serial agent wrote native CLI modules and markdown block/inline rendering modules, then patched parser and renderer behavior after diffs exposed mismatches.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The delivered artifact included test16.mjs plus lib/cli and lib/markdown modules, with program.mjs composing parsed arguments and native markdown rendering.
serial.verification: The serial agent ran many diff checks against the executable for sample cases and edge cases, including help/errors, repeated flags, raw HTML, code spans, links, lists, and hard breaks.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The native renderer remained incomplete for hidden evaluator coverage, producing a failed official result with 17 of 70 samples passing.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel saw the same prompt and stated ESM, .mjs, manual CLI, and no-npm requirements, but its final artifact depended on the reference executable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial saw the same prompt and used those requirements to guide a native ESM implementation with local modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The key requirement difference was not recognition but enforcement: parallel accepted a wrapper around the allowed observation executable, while serial attempted a JS reimplementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split behavior probing to one child while the parent owned implementation, verification, and final delivery.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child delegation and one actor owned the full probe-implement-verify-deliver loop.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's split was narrow and did not lose implementation ownership; the harmful difference came from the parent's implementation and acceptance choice after the probe result.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child returned CLI and markdown findings to the parent, and no evidence shows the handoff was lost, stale, conflicting, or too bulky to use.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial accumulated its own behavior findings and used them directly to plan module boundaries and renderer rules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The contrast is not a bad child brief or result handoff; it is that the parallel parent retained global task context but closed over a wrapper anyway.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel implemented a parser shim plus reference-runner that calls the Python executable via node:child_process.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented native CLI parsing and markdown block/inline rendering in local ESM modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's core behavior remained external to the submitted JS code; serial's core behavior lived in the submitted JS modules.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The single child completed and returned findings before the parent wrote the final files; there was no missing join or trapped verifier result.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results to retrieve and kept findings within the same actor's working context.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Result lifecycle did not explain the failure gap; parallel received its child result and then made a bad global acceptance decision.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel integrated only parent-written files into /output; the problematic shared state was the final dependency on the dataset executable, not a write collision with the child.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial delivered an entrypoint plus CLI and markdown modules without shared-workspace conflicts or subagent provenance issues.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both assembled artifacts, but parallel's assembly included a reference-runner module while serial assembled native markdown modules.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran parity checks that passed because the Node entry delegated behavior to the same executable being used as the oracle, then accepted the whole task.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran many diff checks against the executable, found mismatches, patched renderer logic, and ended with local matches on checked cases.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel verification was circular for the core markdown requirement; serial verification exercised a native implementation, though it did not cover enough hidden cases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel completed quickly with one child and no timeout, then marked all plan steps complete after wrapper parity checks.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used more time and tokens but stayed within budget, completed its plan, and closed after broad local verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no evidence of fan-out or timeout pressure; closure quality differed because parallel accepted a visible task mismatch while serial spent the budget on native behavior coverage.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official relation is both_fail because neither completed evaluation passed: parallel scored 0/70 and serial scored 17/70. The material quality gap is explained by concrete implementation and acceptance differences. Parallel delivered a wrapper that invoked the reference executable, so its local checks did not prove a standalone JavaScript port. Serial delivered a native ESM implementation with explicit markdown parser modules and therefore earned partial hidden-test coverage despite remaining incomplete.
parallel_contributors: Parent accepted a reference-executable wrapper as complete after local parity checks.
Final artifact included reference-runner.mjs and depended on /workspace/dataset/test16_executable.
serial_contributors: Serial wrote native CLI and markdown modules and patched observed renderer defects.
Serial verification covered more real markdown behavior but still missed hidden cases.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel's core implementation choice was a prohibited/non-portable adapter instead of markdown logic.
Serial's native markdown emulator remained incomplete for the official hidden suite.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: Supported comparative contributors to quality gap; not an exclusive root cause and not a pass/fail outcome differential because both runs failed.
